definitions.explanation: Spirited energy or liveliness, especially as expressed outwardly through voice, manner, or attitude. Often used to describe the energetic atmosphere at markets, festivals, or workplaces.

examples.japanese: {威勢|いせい}のいい{掛|か}け{声|ごえ}が{聞|き}こえる。
{魚屋|さかなや}の{店主|てんしゅ}が{威勢|いせい}よく{客|きゃく}を{呼|よ}び{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: The fish shop owner is energetically calling out to customers.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}は{威勢|いせい}がよかったが、だんだん{元気|げんき}がなくなってきた。
examples.english: At first he was full of energy, but gradually he lost his spirit.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the phrase {威勢|いせい}がいい (spirited, energetic) or the adverbial form {威勢|いせい}よく. Associated with the lively atmosphere of traditional Japanese markets and festivals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {威勢|いせい}がいい: spirited, lively, energetic
- {威勢|いせい}よく: vigorously, energetically
- {威勢|いせい}のいい{声|こえ}: spirited voice/shout
- {威勢|いせい}のいい{掛|か}け{声|ごえ}: spirited call/chant
